+---
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9280'
+title: Orderly shutdown suspends the live sessions so working runs stay restorable
+---
+## What
+At an orderly process shutdown the agent must leave working sessions and their runs restorable, like a clean crash. The Router now has a suspending close (Router main 29e7153a): `RoutedSession.suspend()` (nonisolated, idempotent) and `RouterSessionDirectory.suspendLiveSessions()`. After a suspend the journal refuses every `.completed` (the close sweep, a late tool body that swallows the cancel, and `completeClaimedRun` returns false); open claims stay open; runs stay `.orphaned` and claimable. A normal `close()` still cancels the work.
+
+Today (read in the code, not run): `tearDownSession` (`Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Agent/SessionLifecycle.swift`) stops the agent runs (`AgentsMount.runner`) and then closes the root session. At a process shutdown that cancels the working runs and the Router journals the cancellation, so the runs are not restorable. See the Router card "A tool run that the host cancels for a shutdown must not be journaled as succeeded" and the decision of the coordinator: no Extras change; suspend instead.
+
+Do:
+1. Find every path that ends the process or the connection of the agent (a signal, end of stdin, the connection close, the `acp-agent` command exit; see `Sources/acp-agent/InterruptHandler.swift` and the lifecycle code). For an orderly PROCESS shutdown call `RouterSessionDirectory.suspendLiveSessions()` first, then stop the runner and close the sessions. After the suspend, `runner.stop()` must mark nothing ended and post no result mail (the Agents package does this already; see its README).
+2. A USER `session/close` or `session/cancel` is not a shutdown: it keeps the current behavior (cancel the work; the Agents package marks the run ended with reason cancelled).
+3. A connection loss while the agent process lives is not a shutdown of the sessions: do not suspend them (the sessions stay active; ACP lets the agent continue or cancel foreground work; keep the current behavior and say so in a comment).
+4. Write down the shutdown order in `README.md`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] An orderly shutdown with a working nested run leaves the run `.orphaned` in the journal after a reload (use the real Router and a stub model), and the ended marker is not set.
+- [ ] A user `session/close` still cancels the work and marks the run ended.
+- [ ] A shutdown with no live session does nothing special and does not hang.
+- [ ] The shutdown order is in the README.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/OrderlyShutdownTests.swift`.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter OrderlyShutdownTests`. All pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #subagents
\ No newline at end of file

+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Agent/SessionLifecycle.swift:207` `duplication/duplication` — The new shutdown() repeats the close loop and the hook drain of closeSessions(where:). Both loop over the open sessions, call tearDownSession on each one that is not closed, and then await hooks.dispatcher.drain(). +- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Agent/SessionLifecycle.swift:207` `reuse/reuse` — `shutdown()` copies the loop of the existing private `closeSessions(where:)` (it closes each open session with `tearDownSession` and then drains the hook dispatcher). The copy exists only because `closeSessions` cannot pass `isShutdown: true` to `tearDownSession`. The duplicate loop will drift from the original, for example when the selection or drain rules change. Add an `isShutdown: Bool = false` parameter to `closeSessions(where:)` and pass it to `tearDownSession`. Then `shutdown()` becomes `sessionDirectory.suspendLiveSessions()`, then `await closeSessions(where: { _ in true }, isShutdown: true)`, then `await settingsStore.stopWatching()`. This keeps one loop and one drain.
+- [ ] `Sources/acp-agent/AcpCommand.swift:94` `duplication/duplication` — The added call to composed.shutdown() repeats the teardown order that RunPrompt.swift already uses: waitForConnectionTeardown(), then shutdown(). The required order is now written in two places, and a later edit to one copy would not reach the other. Add one method on ComposedAgent, for example `closeAfterConnectionTeardown()`, that calls waitForConnectionTeardown() and then shutdown(). Call it from AcpCommand.swift:93-94 and from RunPrompt.swift:199-200, and delete both copies of the pair.
+- [ ] `Sources/acp-agent/RunPrompt.swift:200` `duplication/duplication` — The added call to composed.shutdown() repeats the two-step teardown order that AcpCommand.swift already uses: waitForConnectionTeardown(), then shutdown(). The required order (wait for the connection teardown first, then shut down) is now written in two places. A later edit to one copy, such as calling shutdown() before the wait, would not reach the other. Add one method on ComposedAgent, for example `closeAfterConnectionTeardown()`, that calls waitForConnectionTeardown() and then shutdown(). Call it from RunPrompt.swift:199-200 and from AcpCommand.swift:93-94, and delete the two copies of the pair.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/OrderlyShutdownTests.swift:69` `swift/concurrency` — The helper starts a detached `Task { ... }` and does not store its handle. The prompt runs for the whole test, and nothing cancels or awaits it. The rule asks for stored Task handles that are cancelled at teardown, so a leaked prompt can outlive the fixture. Keep the handle in the `Working` value, for example `let promptTask: Task<Void, Never>`. Cancel it or await it in the test teardown after `hold.release()`. Or use `async let` if the fixture can await the prompt in structured form.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/OrderlyShutdownTests.swift:70` `test-integrity/no-test-cheating` — The root prompt is sent inside a Task with `try?`, which discards any error from `connection.prompt`. If the prompt fails, the test cannot show why. It only waits until its timeout, so the swallowed failure hides the real cause. Store the Task and await its result with `try await task.value`, or record the error and assert it is nil, so a failed prompt fails the test with its cause.
